title: Can ChatGPT make videos? ChatGPT vs Photoroom's Video Ad Maker
summary: ChatGPT can't make videos on its own, let alone video ads. See how it compares with Photoroom for product video ads, and when each one makes sense.
body_markdown:
You need product videos for your listings and video ads for your campaigns. Your customers are scrolling Instagram, TikTok and YouTube Shorts, where motion stops the thumb and a still photo gets skipped in a second. But you don't have the budget, a studio or a video editor, let alone the time to test what works and what doesn't.


You already use ChatGPT for captions, emails and campaign ideas, so the question comes naturally: **can ChatGPT just make the video for me?**


**The short answer is no, not on its own.** OpenAI discontinued Sora, its video app, on April 26, 2026, and ChatGPT has no built-in video model. Ask it for a video and you'll get a script. And if you sell online, the video you need most is usually an ad. F **or product video ads, a dedicated video tool is the faster route.**


The good news is that you don’t need a shoot or editing skills to get video ads of your products.[Photoroom’s Video Ad Maker](https://www.photoroom.com/tools/video-generator/ad-maker) turns the product photos you already have into video ads, with the shots, script and voiceover planned for you.


This guide compares ChatGPT with Photoroom for product video ads, shows the same ad made with each, and explains when each one makes sense. It also answers the question behind it: is a dedicated video tool like Photoroom better than ChatGPT for your store?


## Why ChatGPT falls short for product video ads


If you try to make a product video ad with ChatGPT, you’ll likely hit one of three walls that slow down your production, your launches and, in the end, your sales.


### 1. You ask for a video and get a script


ChatGPT works with text, and it no longer has a video app of its own.[OpenAI's help center](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/20001152) confirms that "the Sora web and app experiences were discontinued on April 26, 2026", and the Sora API closed in September. So when you ask for a video, ChatGPT describes one: a script, some shot ideas, a caption. You're still left with the hard part, which is making the video.


### 2. ChatGPT can't show your real product


Even with a perfect script, ChatGPT has no way to turn your product into footage. You'd have to film it yourself, or use a tool that generates video from a text description, which shows *a* bottle, *a* sneaker or *a* lamp, not yours. When a shopper can buy the product a few seconds later, a near-match isn't good enough.


### 3. Even a usable clip isn't a finished ad


Say you do get a clip you like. It still needs a voiceover, your offer,[the right shape for each platform](https://www.photoroom.com/blog/ecommerce-video-ads) (vertical for Reels and TikTok, square or 4:5 for the Feed, horizontal for Amazon), and two or three versions to test. Each of those is another tool or another round of work, which is exactly what you were trying to avoid.


## The alternative to ChatGPT: video ads from your product photos


Instead of describing a video to ChatGPT, start from what you already have: your product photos.[Photoroom's Video Ad Maker](https://www.photoroom.com/tools/video-generator/ad-maker) turns them into finished video ads and social media videos, and handles everything ChatGPT leaves to you: the shots, the script, the voiceover, the format for each platform and the next version to test.


1.


**Start from your product photos.** Upload up to four, or pick images already in your Photoroom account. Different angles give the AI more to work with.


2.


**Let Photoroom plan the ad.** You can guide the AI assistant or let it suggest a video type, style and length. It then drafts a shot-by-shot plan, a script and a voiceover. Planning and production happen in the same place.


3.


**Refine it in the chat.** Rewrite a line, swap a shot, change the voice or language, or ask for a different tone before you generate.


4.


**Export for each platform.** Choose 9:16 for Reels, Stories, TikTok and Shorts, or 16:9 for Amazon and product pages, at 5, 8 or 10 seconds. Check the product matches the real item, then upload it to your ad platform or share it on your profiles.


5.


**Make the next version.** Change the hook or the offer and generate again, so you have two or three versions to test from one session.


Because every video starts from your own product photos, **the product in the video matches what customers receive** . And because each version is a quick change rather than a new project, testing stays fast and affordable.

## When to use ChatGPT, and when to use Photoroom


ChatGPT and Photoroom do different jobs. ChatGPT helps you plan: ideas, scripts and copy. Photoroom helps you produce: it turns your product photos into finished video ads in minutes, so you can test new versions, repeat what works and keep your ads fresh without a bigger team or budget.


**ChatGPT is enough when you need to:**


-


Brainstorm hooks, angles and offers for your next campaign


-


Write a script for a video you'll film yourself


-


Draft captions, ad copy and variations to test


-


Plan what to post and when


**You need Photoroom when you need to:**


-


Get a finished video file, not a description of one


-


Show your real product, not a lookalike


-


Publish in the right format for each platform


-


Make new versions often enough to test what works


If your bottleneck is ideas, ChatGPT helps. If your bottleneck is making the videos themselves, quickly and often enough to test, that’s the job Photoroom does.
